title: Simple
coreMove: Strip a message to the one priority that should guide decisions when details collapse.
sourcePressure: The source frames simplicity as core plus compact: Commanders Intent, Southwest Airlines, the Daily Record, proverbs, schemas, and decision-paralysis research all point to forced prioritization that survives real choices.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating simple as shorter wording, a slogan, or dumbed-down messaging.

sourceAnchors.name: Commanders Intent
sourceAnchors.detail: the sidecar says the chapter begins with the militarys Commanders Intent, where detailed plans fail in the field and one compact mission core must survive changing conditions
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: When the field scrambles the plan, Commanders Intent is the sentence people can still carry.

sourceAnchors.name: Southwest Airlines
sourceAnchors.detail: the sidecar names Southwest as the core-business example where a single low-fare priority helps employees resolve local tradeoffs without central instruction
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Southwests low-fare priority works because it settles tradeoffs before the next local question arrives.

sourceAnchors.name: Hoover Adams
sourceAnchors.detail: the sidecar names the Daily Record and Hoover Adams as support for a memorable editorial core beating daily decision paralysis
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Hoover Adams shows the same discipline in a newsroom: the local core tells people what deserves space.

hook: A cluttered meeting opens every simplicity lesson
The message is buried under too many slides
counterintuition: simple is not simplistic as a standalone thesis
less is more without a decision test
tryThisNow: write one sentence about your message
set a timer and cut words
examples: slide deck pruning as the only scene

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.audience: a charge nurse trying to align a rotating night team
exampleSpecs.stakes: a full waiting room and three competing priorities during a storm surge
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Sarah erases four color codes from the board and leaves one red tag rule that tells the float nurse which patient moves first
exampleSpecs.firstImage: rainwater pooled under the ambulance-bay doors while the triage board glows blue

exampleSpecs.audience: a public-works supervisor briefing contractors before first snow
exampleSpecs.stakes: school buses and dialysis pickups depend on the same two-lane roads
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Mathieu circles the school and clinic routes in black and tells every driver that those roads beat complaints from side streets
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a salt-streaked map spread across a folding table at 4:42 a.m.

exampleSpecs.audience: a buyer with limited shelf space before holiday ordering
exampleSpecs.stakes: cash tied up in unsold inventory can decide January payroll
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Ingrid pulls every maybe title from the cart and keeps only books that serve the stores local-gift identity
exampleSpecs.firstImage: the smell of cardboard and pine-scented candles behind the register

exampleSpecs.audience: a stage manager coordinating volunteers and teenage actors
exampleSpecs.stakes: a blackout scene can injure someone if everyone follows separate cues
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Daniel stops the cue-by-cue lecture and makes the single rule hands off the stairs until work lights are up
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Nobody moves on the stairs until I call white light," Daniel says into the empty house

exampleSpecs.audience: a new manager training weekend staff in a crowded market hall
exampleSpecs.stakes: health inspection risk and line speed collide before noon
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Catarina realizes the staff need one priority, keep cold stock cold, before they learn the whole display ritual
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Catarina three Saturdays to see why the checklist kept failing

exampleSpecs.audience: a curator cutting an overstuffed tour for first-time visitors
exampleSpecs.stakes: visitors quit after room two if every object gets equal importance
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Akira chooses the one question each gallery should answer and removes every clip that does not serve it
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What should a visitor remember after the headphones come off?

skillTargets: identify the core that should govern a messy decision
choose a schema that preserves the real constraint
diagnose when too many priorities block local action

tryThisNowSpec: Take one message you need someone to act on and write the tradeoff it should settle, then delete any word that does not help settle that tradeoff.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
